person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: Cognitive load in undergraduates using AR for science learning, and how it relates to their self-efficacy and observed learning behaviour.
span.quote: Thus, this study aimed to identify undergraduate students’ profiles of cognitive load in AR-assisted science learning and to examine the role of their distinct profiles in self-efficacy together with associated behavior patterns in science learning.

span.label: Do students split into distinct cognitive-load types rather than lying on one scale, and if so do those types differ in self-efficacy and in what they actually do?
span.quote: However, to the best of our knowledge, exploration of the relationship between students’ multi-dimensional profiles of cognitive load in AR-assisted science learning, self-efficacy, and the associated behavior patterns is still rare in the literature.

span.label: Four cognitive-load profiles - Low Engagement, Immersive, Dabbling, Organized - that differ measurably in self-efficacy and in behaviour sequences.
span.quote: The latent profile analysis findings revealed four fundamental profiles: Low Engagement, Immersive, Dabbling, and Organized, characterized as carrying various respective cognitive loads.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The latent profile analysis findings revealed four fundamental profiles: Low Engagement, Immersive, Dabbling, and Organized, characterized as carrying various respective cognitive loads.

span.label: cognitive load in augmented-reality science learning
span.quote: Thus, this study aimed to identify undergraduate students’ profiles of cognitive load in AR-assisted science learning and to examine the role of their distinct profiles in self-efficacy together with associated behavior patterns in science learning.

span.label: survey-study
span.quote: After ensuring the validity and reliability of each measure, a latent profile analysis confirmed that 365 Chinese undergraduates carried diverse dimensions of cognitive load simultaneously.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Collaborating and discussing with peers distributes the information-processing burden between students, which lowers each student's mental load and frees effort for performance
span.quote: When they discussed scientific issues or provided assistance to each other, they shared the burden of information processing with each other, which decreased their mental load.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The transaction costs of collaborating are themselves effortful, so heavy interaction can push cognitive processing into overload rather than relieving it
span.quote: When communication and collaboration require students to invest considerable mental effort, high transaction costs in interactions may overload their cognitive process.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: cognitive load is treated as multi-dimensional, so a learner can be high on one dimension and low on another - which is why a single scale hides the types
span.quote: Cognitive load is a multi-dimensional cognitive construct representing load when doing a particular task (Paas & van Merriënboer, 1994 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: extraneous load comes from how the material was designed rather than from its difficulty, so it is the component an instructor can remove
span.quote: Extraneous cognitive load is caused by the poor design of instructional materials, which requires extra cognitive handling (Kirschner et al., 2006 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: self-efficacy is proposed as the link between load and outcome: a sense of competence assists the cognitive processing itself
span.quote: students with high self-efficacy may have a powerful sense of competence, which may assist in cognitive processes (Lin et al., 2020 ), academic performance (Wang et al., 2018 ), and achievement (Chang et al., 2018 )

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AR adds load as well as benefit - multitasking between the virtual and real layers pulls attention off the instructions
span.quote: In addition, multitasking is another issue related to the AR learning system, which can be a distraction factor that will lead students to ignore the instructions in their learning process (Garzón et al., 2019 ).

span.label: The profiles rest on only three self-reported cognitive-load dimensions within AR-based activities
span.quote: The first is that the AR cognitive load learning profiles were focused on AR-based learning activities and three types of cognitive load: mental load, mental effort, and performance.

span.label: Objective process measures such as eye and hand movement tracking were not collected and are needed to characterise the visual and motor behaviour behind the cognitive load
span.quote: Notably, other measures of cognitive processes, such as eye and hand movement tracking, may need to be considered for future study to elucidate understanding of the students’ visual and movement behavior, resulting in their cognitive load in the AR-assisted science learning environment.

span.label: The literature it builds on disagrees with itself about the sign of the effect - more load has been reported as better, worse and neutral.
span.quote: For example, students processing more cognitive load may perform better (Lai et al., 2019 ; Thees et al., 2020 ), less favorably (Sung et al., 2014 ; Thees et al., 2020 ), or with no significant difference (Hwang et al., 2018 ; Wu et al., 2018 ) between the experimental and control groups.

span.label: The three classical load types are stated to be an incomplete account, and the paper adopts a second framework alongside them rather than resolving the conflict.
span.quote: However, these three classical types only give a partial picture of cognitive load (Xie & Salvendy, 2000 ), and do not properly capture the mental effort-based aspect of cognitive load (Feldon, 2007 ).

span.label: One cohort, one country, one task - 365 Chinese undergraduates in a single AR activity.
span.quote: a latent profile analysis confirmed that 365 Chinese undergraduates carried diverse dimensions of cognitive load simultaneously

span.label: an LSTM plus convolutional-neural-network architecture, imported to classify students' coded learning-behaviour sequences
span.quote: Long short-term memory (LSTM) and the convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithm architecture were applied to identify behavioral sequences based on the data.

span.label: working memory as a capacity limit, used to define germane load and thereby to ground an instructional-design construct in a memory construct
span.quote: Germane cognitive load is defined as the amount of working memory capacity required for managing intrinsic load.

span.label: cognitive load - Sweller's decomposition into three TYPES by source: intrinsic, extraneous, germane
span.quote: First, Sweller ( 1988 ) identified three types of cognitive load—intrinsic, extraneous, and germane—focusing on the interpretation of performance and task-based measures.

span.label: cognitive load - Paas and van Merrienboer's decomposition into three DIMENSIONS of assessment: mental load, mental effort, performance
span.quote: According to their theory, cognitive load is supposed to be assessed according to three dimensions: mental load, mental effort, and performance.

span.label: load - as something a learner can have more or less of, where the literature disagrees even about whether more is better
span.quote: For example, students processing more cognitive load may perform better (Lai et al., 2019 ; Thees et al., 2020 ), less favorably (Sung et al., 2014 ; Thees et al., 2020 ), or with no significant difference (Hwang et al., 2018 ; Wu et al., 2018 ) between the experimental and control groups.

span.label: extends → Thees et al. (2020)
span.quote: Therefore, this study included self-efficacy as a factor to identify the underlying subgroups in AR-assisted science learning regarding students’ cognitive load, unlike previous studies (e.g. Thees et al., 2020 ), which only proved the effect of an AR-assisted learning system on science learning performance and cognitive load.

span.label: replicates → Lin et al. (2020)
span.quote: This result is consistent with Lin et al.’s ( 2020 ) verified assumptions that hands-on activity using AR boosts students’ understanding of scientific concepts.

span.label: builds-on → Chin and Wang (2021)
span.quote: This study provides further evidence for the study of Chin and Wang ( 2021 ), who revealed that AR technology could provide different authentic learning activities for students to understand the difficulties (e.g. cognitive overload) in learning.

span.label: builds-on → Sweller (1988), the three types of cognitive load
span.quote: First, Sweller ( 1988 ) identified three types of cognitive load—intrinsic, extraneous, and germane—focusing on the interpretation of performance and task-based measures.

span.label: builds-on → Paas and van Merrienboer (1994), cognitive load as three dimensions of assessment
span.quote: According to their theory, cognitive load is supposed to be assessed according to three dimensions: mental load, mental effort, and performance.

span.label: contradicts → the assumption that one AR learning design suits all students
span.quote: previous researchers also indicate that a specific type of AR-assisted science learning design or support may not suit or be effective for all students because students’ cognitive load may differ according to their experiences and individual characteristics (Thees et al., 2020 )

span.label: RETRACTED (WRONG TYPE: a KIND, not a PART) · intrinsic cognitive load —part-of→ cognitive load
span.quote: First, Sweller ( 1988 ) identified three types of cognitive load—intrinsic, extraneous, and germane—focusing on the interpretation of performance and task-based measures.

span.label: RETRACTED (WRONG TYPE: a KIND, not a PART) · extraneous cognitive load —part-of→ cognitive load
span.quote: First, Sweller ( 1988 ) identified three types of cognitive load—intrinsic, extraneous, and germane—focusing on the interpretation of performance and task-based measures.

span.label: germane cognitive load —operationalised-as→ working memory
span.quote: Germane cognitive load is defined as the amount of working memory capacity required for managing intrinsic load.

span.label: extraneous cognitive load —distinct-from→ intrinsic cognitive load
span.quote: First, Sweller ( 1988 ) identified three types of cognitive load—intrinsic, extraneous, and germane—focusing on the interpretation of performance and task-based measures.

span.label: mental effort —part-of→ cognitive load
span.quote: According to their theory, cognitive load is supposed to be assessed according to three dimensions: mental load, mental effort, and performance.

span.label: augmented reality —causes→ cognitive load
span.quote: In addition, multitasking is another issue related to the AR learning system, which can be a distraction factor that will lead students to ignore the instructions in their learning process (Garzón et al., 2019 ).

span.label: intrinsic cognitive load —is-a→ cognitive load
span.quote: First, Sweller ( 1988 ) identified three types of cognitive load—intrinsic, extraneous, and germane—focusing on the interpretation of performance and task-based measures.

span.label: extraneous cognitive load —is-a→ cognitive load
span.quote: First, Sweller ( 1988 ) identified three types of cognitive load—intrinsic, extraneous, and germane—focusing on the interpretation of performance and task-based measures.

span.label: latent profile analysis
span.quote: Third, in order to identify latent profiles of the students’ AR-assisted science learning data, a statistical method of latent profile analysis of cognitive load data set (i.e. mental effort, mental load, and performance) was conducted for analyzing as continuous observed variables to identify unobservable groups among subjects.

span.label: confirmatory factor analysis
span.quote: Second, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) validated the constructs of the two instruments using Mplus 7.4.

span.label: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
span.quote: First, a Kolmogorov–Smirnov test was conducted to test the data distributions, indicating the data was not normally distributed.

span.label: Cronbach's alpha
span.quote: In this study, the Cronbach’s alpha values of mental load, mental effort, and performance are 0.92, 0.92, and 0.85, respectively, indicating that the scale is reliable.

span.label: MANOVA
span.quote: Finally, this study conducted a multivariate analysis of variance to compare the differences between the identified unobservable subgroups of the students’ cognitive load and their role in AR science learning self-efficacy.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: The multivariate analysis of variance indicated that the four profiles were significantly different

span.label: Cohen's kappa (inter-rater reliability)
span.quote: The inter-rater reliability kappa of the two teachers’ analytic results was 0.82

span.label: lag sequential analysis
span.quote: This study performed a lag sequential analysis to examine the students’ learning behavior patterns from the AR-assisted science learning system.

span.label: z-score (adjusted residual)
span.quote: Statistical significance was analyzed by calculating Z-score (an adjusted residual value) statistics using a sequential pattern analysis program (GSEQ 5.1).

span.label: chi-squared / model fit indices
span.quote: According to the suggestion indices proposed by Marsh et al. ( 2004 ), the three-factor structure of cognitive load scales in the AR context fitted well

span.label: bootstrap likelihood ratio test
span.quote: The bootstrap likelihood ratio test and adjusted Lo-Mendell-Rubin test were also considered (Lo et al., 2001 ).

span.label: information criteria (AIC / adjusted BIC) and entropy
span.term: information criteria (AIC / adjusted BIC) and entropy
span.quote: The low values of the Akaike information criterion, adjusted Bayesian information criterion, and higher entropy indicated that the models’ fits were good (Burnham & Anderson, 2002 ).

span.label: post hoc test
span.quote: Moreover, post hoc tests indicated that only profiles 3 and 4 were not significantly different in the dimensions of AR science learning self-efficacy, excluding conceptual understanding and higher-order cognitive skills.

span.label: latent-profile-analysis
span.quote: a latent profile analysis confirmed that 365 Chinese undergraduates carried diverse dimensions of cognitive load simultaneously

span.label: anova
span.quote: The multivariate analysis of variance findings revealed different levels of the six AR science learning self-efficacy dimensions across profiles.

span.label: statistical-significance
span.quote: The lag sequential analysis results showed significant differences in behavior patterns among profiles.

span.label: Latent profile analysis of three cognitive-load dimensions sorted the undergraduates into four profiles, named Low Engagement, Immersive, Dabbling and Organized.
span.quote: The latent profile analysis findings revealed four fundamental profiles: Low Engagement, Immersive, Dabbling, and Organized, characterized as carrying various respective cognitive loads.

span.label: The Immersive profile (100 students) combined the highest mental effort with the lowest mental load and the second-highest performance of the four profiles.
span.quote: In profile 2, 100 participants attained the highest mean values for mental effort, second-highest mean values for performance, and lowest mean values for mental load across the four profiles.

span.label: Immersive-profile students reported the highest science learning self-efficacy of any profile.
span.quote: Students with the Immersive profile had the highest science learning self-efficacy.

span.label: Low Engagement students scored lowest on every self-efficacy dimension measured.
span.quote: Low Engagement students displayed the lowest self-efficacy among all dimensions.

span.label: Organized-profile students outscored Dabbling students specifically on conceptual understanding and higher-order cognitive skills.
span.quote: Organized students recorded better conceptual understanding and higher-order cognitive skills than Dabbling ones.

span.label: Profiles whose behaviour sequences included discussing with peers, taking tests and reading feedback had significantly higher self-efficacy than profiles whose behaviour was mainly taking tests and visiting resources.
span.quote: Among them, profiles with social interaction, test, and reviewing feedback behavior had a significantly higher score for self-efficacy than those patterns mainly based on test learning and resource visits.

span.label: The four-profile solution was preferred because it had the lowest AIC and adjusted BIC once the five-profile model was ruled out for containing a group under 10% of participants.
span.quote: Excluding the five-profile model, Akaike information criterion and adjusted Bayesian information criterion were the lowest for the four-profile model among all other models.

span.label: Dabbling and Organized students differed significantly only on conceptual understanding and higher-order cognitive skills, not on the other four self-efficacy dimensions.
span.quote: Moreover, post hoc tests indicated that only profiles 3 and 4 were not significantly different in the dimensions of AR science learning self-efficacy, excluding conceptual understanding and higher-order cognitive skills.

span.label: The Organized profile achieved the highest performance of all four profiles while carrying high mental effort and only medium mental load, alongside more communicative and collaborative behaviour.
span.quote: Students with the Organized profile showed the highest performance among other profiles, with a high level of mental effort, medium level of mental load, and more communicative and collaborative behaviors.

span.label: Organized and Dabbling students, though similar in mental load, differed behaviourally in that Organized students finished tasks progressively while Dabbling students re-browsed materials and retried tasks with new answers.
span.quote: Based on behavior patterns, it appeared that the key difference between the two profiles was that students in profile 4 progressively finished the tasks, while those in profile 3 kept repeatedly browsing learning materials and trying to complete the tasks with new answers.

span.label: Learners fall into four cognitive-load types rather than varying along one dimension.
span.quote: The latent profile analysis findings revealed four fundamental profiles: Low Engagement, Immersive, Dabbling, and Organized, characterized as carrying various respective cognitive loads.

span.label: The profiles differ in self-efficacy, with Low Engagement lowest on every dimension and Immersive highest overall.
span.quote: Students with the Immersive profile had the highest science learning self-efficacy.

span.label: Organized learners outperformed Dabbling ones on conceptual understanding and higher-order skills.
span.quote: Organized students recorded better conceptual understanding and higher-order cognitive skills than Dabbling ones.

span.label: What students actually did differed by profile, and the sequences involving social interaction and reviewing feedback went with higher self-efficacy than test-and-browse sequences.
span.quote: Among them, profiles with social interaction, test, and reviewing feedback behavior had a significantly higher score for self-efficacy than those patterns mainly based on test learning and resource visits.
